Affiant: Desmond Anthony Reid
Re: Marcia Evadne Whitfield, A# [A-NUMBER]
Form I-360 VAWA Self-Petition
I, Desmond Anthony Reid, being of legal age, state the following:
1. My name is Desmond Anthony Reid. I was born on October 21, 1981, in Spanish Town, St.
Catherine, Jamaica. I am a naturalized United States citizen. I live at 72 Halsted Street, East Orange,
New Jersey 07018. My telephone number is [PHONE].
2. I make this affidavit in support of the self-petition of my friend, Marcia Evadne Whitfield.
Everything I state here is based on my own personal knowledge, except where I say that Marcia told
me something.
3. I have known Marcia for about twenty years. We met as young adults at church in Spanish Town
and became good friends. After she came to New Jersey in 2018, we reconnected, and she has been
like family to me ever since.
4. I know Vernon Lloyd Lattimore because we worked together for several years as forklift operators
at a distribution warehouse. We were friendly at work and sometimes got together on weekends.
5. I am the one who introduced Marcia and Vernon. I invited both of them to my birthday party on
October 21, 2021, at my home in East Orange, and I introduced them to each other that evening.
They talked for most of the night, and before long they were dating. At the time I thought Vernon
was a good man and that they would be good for each other. I regret that now.
6. Over the following months I saw Marcia and Vernon together often. They came to my home
together, and I saw them at gatherings with friends. Vernon told me more than once that he had
found the woman he wanted to marry. Marcia was very happy, and I could see that she loved him.
7. I attended their wedding at East Orange City Hall on July 15, 2022, and the dinner afterward. After
the wedding, Marcia moved into Vernon's apartment on Prospect Street in East Orange. I visited
them there several times, including for Thanksgiving dinner in November 2022. They lived there
together as husband and wife.
8. I have no doubt that Marcia married Vernon because she loved him. She talked about buying a
house and starting a life with him. She never gave me any reason to think she married him for
immigration papers.
9. I left the warehouse in 2023 for a job closer to home, so I saw Vernon less often after that. In
March 2024, Marcia called me upset and told me that Vernon had been fired from the warehouse in
February and had hidden it from her for weeks, leaving the house every morning as if he was going
to work. I was very surprised that he would keep something like that from his wife.
10. After their wedding, I personally never saw Vernon hit Marcia or argue with her. When I was
around them, things seemed normal. However, during 2024 I noticed that Marcia changed. She
","Page 2 of 2
stopped coming to church, she did not return my calls as often, and when I did see her she seemed
quiet, tired, and sad. She was not the cheerful person I had known for most of my life.
11. In 2025, Marcia told me what had been happening at home. She told me that Vernon stopped
working and made her pay all the bills, that he yelled at her and called her terrible names, that he
took money from their account, and that he spat on her during an argument. She also told me that
he refused to go to her immigration interview and later moved out. She cried while telling me these
things. I have known Marcia for twenty years, and I have never known her to lie. I believe her.
12. After Vernon moved out, I tried to call him to talk to him about how he treated Marcia, but he
did not answer my calls.
13. Marcia is an honest, hardworking, and kind person. I respectfully ask that her petition be
approved.
I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the foregoing
is true and correct.
Signature: _________________________________

Place: East Orange, NJ

 AFFIDAVIT OF MARCIA EVADNE WHITFIELD
 In Support of Form I-360, Petition for Amerasian, Widow(er), or Special Immigrant
 (VAWA Self-Petitioning Spouse of a U.S. Citizen)
 A-Number: [A-NUMBER]
I, Marcia Evadne Whitfield, declare as follows:
About Me
1.   My name is Marcia Evadne Whitfield. I was born on March 14, 1984, in Spanish Town, St.
 Catherine, Jamaica. I am a citizen of Jamaica. I live at 418 Prospect Street, Apartment
3B, East Orange, New Jersey 07017. My A-Number is [A-NUMBER].
2.   I make this affidavit in support of my Form I-360 self-petition as the abused spouse of a
 United States citizen, Vernon Lloyd Lattimore. Everything I state here is based on my
own personal knowledge. I read and understand English, which is my first language.
3.   I came to the United States on August 2, 2018, in J-2 status as the dependent spouse of my
 first husband, who came here as a J-1 research scholar. I worked as a home health aide
with the employment authorization I had as a J-2. My first marriage ended in divorce in
June 2021 in Essex County, New Jersey. We simply grew apart, and the divorce was not
contested. We had no children.
How I Met Vernon and Our Marriage
4.   I met Vernon on Saturday, October 23, 2021, at a birthday gathering for my longtime
 friend Desmond Reid at Desmond's home in East Orange. Desmond and I have known
each other for about twenty years, since we were young people in Spanish Town. Vernon
was a friend of Desmond's from work, and Desmond introduced us that evening. Vernon
was funny and very attentive. He asked for my number before he left.
5.   Vernon and I began seeing each other in November 2021. We went to dinner, to the
 movies, and on long drives down the Shore. He came with me to church a few times and
met my cousin Simone Barrett when she visited from Brooklyn for Christmas. He told me
he wanted a wife and a real home. In March 2022 he asked me to marry him, and I said
yes because I loved him and wanted to build a life with him.
6.   We married on July 15, 2022, at East Orange City Hall. Desmond and Simone were there,
 and afterward we had a small dinner with about fifteen family members and friends. On
the day of our wedding I moved into Vernon's apartment at 418 Prospect Street,
Apartment 3B, and my name was added to the lease. We opened a joint bank account and
shared all of our household bills.
","Affidavit of Marcia Evadne Whitfield – Page 2
7.   In August 2022, Vernon filed a petition for me so that I could become a permanent
 resident, and I filed my application to adjust status at the same time. When we were
preparing the papers, I asked Vernon to pick up certified copies of our marriage
certificate from the city registrar. He came home with a certificate for a different couple.
When I pointed it out, he became embarrassed and finally admitted that he could barely
read. He had hidden this from me the whole time we were dating. I was hurt that he had
kept such a big thing from me, but I told him it did not change how I felt and offered to
help him. For the first year and a half of our marriage we were mostly happy.
How Vernon Changed
8.   Vernon worked as a forklift operator at a distribution warehouse. In February 2024 he lost
 that job, but he did not tell me. For about three weeks he left the apartment every morning
at the usual time as if he were going to work. In early March 2024, I ran into one of his
coworkers at the supermarket, and he asked me how Vernon was doing since he was let
go. I was shocked.
9.   That evening I asked Vernon why he had lied to me. He jumped up, pointed his finger right
 in my face, and shouted that it was his business and not mine. He was so close and so
loud that I backed into the kitchen counter. I had never seen him like that, and I was
frightened.
10.   After that, Vernon changed completely. He slept until noon or later and did not look for
 work. I was working long shifts as a home health aide, and he expected me to pay the rent
and all the bills, and also to cook, clean, and do the laundry. If dinner was not ready when
he wanted it, he would yell at me. He called my food "slop" and "garbage," pushed his
plate away, and told me I could not do anything right. He called me "stupid," "useless,"
and "worthless," and other vulgar names that I am ashamed to repeat. He said no other
man would ever want me.
11.   Vernon began staying out late, and sometimes all night. In June 2024, after he had not
 come home or answered his phone for most of the night, I went looking for him at the
house of his friend Marlon in Irvington. When I came to the door, Vernon came outside
and screamed at me in front of his friends to stop embarrassing him and to stop tracking
him down like a child. His friends were laughing. I drove home crying and humiliated.
12.   During this time Vernon still demanded sex from me, even when I told him I was
 exhausted from work or did not want to. When I said no, he would get angry, sulk, and
accuse me of being with someone else, so I gave in to avoid a fight. I believed he was
seeing another woman, because he was out all night and hid his phone from me. I felt
betrayed and degraded, and I was afraid he would give me a disease. I went to my doctor
to be tested because I was so worried.
","Affidavit of Marcia Evadne Whitfield – Page 3
13.   My cousin Simone and I talk by phone almost every Sunday. Many times during 2024 she
 heard Vernon in the background shouting at me and calling me names. She would ask me
what was going on and tell me I did not deserve to be treated that way. I usually made
excuses for him, because I was ashamed.
14.   In August 2024, I noticed that $600 had been taken out of our joint account, which was
 money I had put aside for the rent. When I asked Vernon about it, he said he had lent it to
a friend. I told him we could not afford that. He got in my face, cursed at me, and spat on
me. The spit hit my face and my neck. I went into the bathroom and locked the door. I
cannot describe how dirty and small that made me feel.
Money, Lies, and My Immigration Case
15.   Vernon controlled our money even though he was not earning it. My paycheck went into
 our joint account, and he kept withdrawing cash and lending money to his friends while I
was struggling to pay the rent and the light bill. In early 2025 we received a notice that
our joint federal tax refund had been taken to pay an old debt of Vernon's that he had
never told me about. When I asked him about it, he told me to mind my business and that
it was "his name, his money."
16.   Vernon knew how important my immigration case was to me, and he began to use it
 against me. When I complained about how he treated me, he would say that I needed him
for my green card and that he could have me sent back to Jamaica whenever he wanted.
Our adjustment interview was scheduled for April 2025. On the morning of the interview,
Vernon refused to come. USCIS rescheduled the interview for later that month, and he
again did not show up. He told me, "Why should I help you get your papers?"
17.   On May 17, 2025, while I was at work, Vernon moved out of the apartment. He took the
 television and some of the furniture and withdrew most of the money left in our account.
He has not answered my calls or messages since then. As far as I know, he is staying with
friends. We are separated but we have not divorced. I have remained in the apartment and
I am paying the rent on my own.
How This Has Affected Me
18.   Living with Vernon's abuse has changed me. I used to be outgoing and active in my
 church. During 2024 and 2025 I withdrew from my friends and stopped going to church
because I was ashamed and did not want anyone to see how unhappy I was. I have trouble
sleeping, I cry often, and I lost my appetite and weight. I still jump when I hear a loud
voice, and I feel nervous when I hear keys at the door, even though Vernon is gone.
19.   I never called the police on Vernon. I was ashamed, and I did not think the police would
 care about yelling and name-calling. I was also afraid that calling the police would make
things worse at home and might hurt my immigration case. In June 2025, my primary
","Affidavit of Marcia Evadne Whitfield – Page 4
care doctor referred me to a licensed clinical social worker, Mr. Gregory Hale, and I have
been seeing him since then. Talking to him helped me understand that what Vernon did to
me was abuse, and that it was not my fault.
Conclusion
20.   I married Vernon because I loved him and wanted to spend my life with him, not to get
 immigration status. I lived with him as his wife from July 15, 2022, until May 17, 2025. I
have never been arrested or charged with any crime in the United States or in any other
country.
21.   I respectfully ask that my self-petition be approved so that I can continue to rebuild my
 life safely in the United States.
I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the
foregoing is true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief.
Executed on October 20, 2025, in East Orange, New Jersey.
October 20, 2025
Marcia Evadne Whitfield

Chapter 1 - Purpose and Background
A. Purpose
The Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (VAWA) amended the nation’s immigration laws and included a broad range of criminal, civil, and
health-related provisions.[1] VAWA addressed the unique issues faced by victims of domestic violence and abuse and provided certain alien family
members of abusive U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents (LPRs) the ability to self-petition for immigrant classification without the
abuser’s knowledge, consent, or participation in the immigration process. This allowed victims to seek both safety and independence from their
abuser.
Spouses, children, and parents of U.S. citizens and spouses and children of LPRs may file a self-petition for immigrant classification with USCIS.
An alien filing the self-petition is generally known as a VAWA self-petitioner.[2] If USCIS approves the self-petition, VAWA self-petitioners may then
seek an immigrant visa from outside the United States or apply for adjustment of status inside the United States.[3]
B. Background
Under the family-based immigration process, U.S. citizens and LPRs may petition for certain categories of relatives to immigrate to the United

A. Filing Requirements and Initial Review
An alien seeking to self-petition under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) must properly file a Petition for Amerasian, Widow(er), or Special
Immigrant (Form I-360) with supporting evidence in accordance with the Form I-360 instructions.[1] USCIS considers Form I-360 as properly filed
if it:
Is submitted on the current edition of the form;
Is filed at the correct filing location; and
Has a valid signature.[2]
When initially reviewing the Form I-360, USCIS first determines whether the Form I-360 has been properly filed according to the above criteria. If
the self-petition is not properly filed, USCIS rejects the filing and returns it to the self-petitioner.[3] If the self-petition is properly filed, USCIS sends
the self-petitioner a receipt notice with a receipt, or filing, date. There is no fee when Form I-360 is filed as a VAWA self-petition.[4] USCIS officers
adhere to current agency guidance and procedures regarding signature requirements.[5]
Self-petitioning spouses, children, and parents of U.S. citizens may seek to adjust status as immediate relatives by filing an Application to Register
Permanent Residence or Adjust Status (Form I-485) at any time, because visas are immediately available for immediate relatives.[6]

Chapter 5 - Adjudication
A. Prima Facie Review
After receipting a self-petition, USCIS first determines whether the evidence submitted establishes a prima facie (“at first look”) case.[1] Self-
petitioning spouses and children and any listed derivative beneficiaries may be considered “qualified aliens” eligible for certain public benefits if
they can establish a prima facie case for immigrant classification or have an approved self-petition.[2]
USCIS does not make a prima facie determination for self-petitions filed from outside the United States. Self-petitioners who are outside the
United States are not eligible for U.S. public benefits. Although USCIS issues prima facie determinations for self-petitioning parents of U.S.
citizens, they are not included in the definition of “qualified aliens” in statute and are, therefore, ineligible for public benefits as “qualified aliens.”[3]
1. Establishing a Prima Facie Case

### II. LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND STANDARD OF PROOF

Under INA § 204(a)(1)(A)(iii) and 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(1), a self-petitioning spouse of a U.S. citizen must establish each of the following eligibility requirements (`USCIS_Policy_Manual_Volume_3_Part_D_VAWA.pdf`, 3 USCIS-PM D.2(A), PDF p. 6 / PM p. 947):
1. **Proper Filing:** The Form I-360 is properly completed, signed, and filed in accordance with form instructions (3 USCIS-PM D.4(A), PDF p. 47 / PM p. 1008).
2. **Qualifying Relationship:** The self-petitioner has a qualifying marital relationship to an abusive U.S. citizen spouse (3 USCIS-PM D.2(B)(1)–(2), PDF pp. 7–10 / PM pp. 948–951).
3. **Eligibility for Immigrant Classification:** The self-petitioner is eligible for immigrant classification as an immediate relative under INA § 201(b)(2)(A)(i) and is not barred under INA §§ 204(c), 204(g), or 204(a)(2) (3 USCIS-PM D.2(D), PDF pp. 21–22 / PM pp. 962–963).
4. **Good-Faith Marriage:** The self-petitioner entered into the qualifying marriage in good faith and not for the purpose of evading immigration laws (3 USCIS-PM D.2(C), PDF pp. 20–21 / PM pp. 961–962).
5. **Battery or Extreme Cruelty:** During the qualifying marriage, the self-petitioner was battered or subjected to extreme cruelty perpetrated by the U.S. citizen spouse (3 USCIS-PM D.2(E), PDF pp. 22–26 / PM pp. 963–967).
6. **Joint Residence:** The self-petitioner resides or has resided with the abusive U.S. citizen spouse during the qualifying relationship (3 USCIS-PM D.2(F), PDF pp. 26–27 / PM pp. 967–968).
7. **Good Moral Character:** The self-petitioner is a person of good moral character (3 USCIS-PM D.2(G), PDF pp. 27–32 / PM pp. 968–973).

* **Standard of Proof:** The burden of proof rests on the self-petitioner to establish eligibility by a **preponderance of the evidence**, meaning that the claimed facts are "more likely than not" or "probably" true (`USCIS_Policy_Manual_Volume_3_Part_D_VAWA.pdf`, 3 USCIS-PM D.2(A), PDF p. 7 / PM p. 948; 3 USCIS-PM D.5(B)(1), PDF p. 52 / PM p. 1013; citing *Matter of Chawathe*, 25 I&N Dec. 369, 376 (AAO 2010)).
* **Any Credible Evidence Provision:** Pursuant to INA § 204(a)(1)(J) and 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(2)(i), USCIS must consider "any credible evidence" relevant to the self-petition, while retaining sole discretion to determine what evidence is credible and the weight to afford that evidence (`USCIS_Policy_Manual_Volume_3_Part_D_VAWA.pdf`, 3 USCIS-PM D.2(A), PDF p. 7 / PM p. 948; 3 USCIS-PM D.5(B)(2), PDF pp. 53–55 / PM pp. 1014–1016). A self-petition may not be denied for failure to submit a particular type or piece of evidence (3 USCIS-PM D.5(B)(2), PDF pp. 53, 55 / PM pp. 1014, 1016). Officers evaluate each piece of evidence individually and in the totality of the circumstances for relevance, probative value, internal and external consistency, detail, and corroboration.

Under INA § 204(a)(1)(A)(iii)(II)(dd), 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(1)(v), and 3 USCIS-PM D.2(F) (PDF pp. 26–27 / PM pp. 967–968), the self-petitioner must reside or have resided with the abuser during the qualifying relationship, though she need not reside with the abuser at the time of filing.
* Pre-review established the joint residency requirement.
* Form I-360 (`I-360_Whitfield.pdf`, Part 10, Items 9–11, p. 14) and the petitioner's affidavit (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 1, ¶ 6; p. 3, ¶ 17; p. 4, ¶ 20) consistently state that the couple resided together at 418 Prospect Street, Apartment 3B, East Orange, NJ 07017, from their wedding date of July 15, 2022, until Mr. Lattimore moved out on May 17, 2025—a period of nearly three years during the qualifying marriage. This shared residence is corroborated by eyewitness visits by Mr. Reid (`Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, p. 1, ¶ 7) and Ms. Barrett (`Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 10).

#### 6. Subjected to Battery or Extreme Cruelty (3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)) — **MET**
Under INA § 204(a)(1)(A)(iii)(I)(bb), 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(1)(vi), and 3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)(1) (PDF pp. 22–26 / PM pp. 963–967), the self-petitioner must establish that her U.S. citizen spouse battered her or subjected her to extreme cruelty during the qualifying marriage. Based on a holistic evaluation of the record, the self-petitioner has established **both** battery and extreme cruelty by a preponderance of the evidence.

##### A. Finding of Battery
The USCIS Policy Manual defines battery as follows:
> "Battery generally includes any offensive touching or use of force on a person without the person’s consent. Some examples include, but are not limited to, punching, slapping, **spitting**, biting, kicking, choking, kidnapping, rape, molestation, forced prostitution, sexual abuse, and sexual exploitation." (`USCIS_Policy_Manual_Volume_3_Part_D_VAWA.pdf`, 3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)(1), PDF p. 24 / PM p. 965).

* **August 2024 Spitting Incident:** In her affidavit, the petitioner provides a detailed account that in August 2024—during the qualifying marriage and while residing together—she noticed that $600 she had set aside for rent had been withdrawn from their joint bank account (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 14). When she told Mr. Lattimore that they could not afford for him to lend the rent money to a friend, Mr. Lattimore got in her face, cursed at her, and **spat on her**, hitting her face and neck, causing her to flee into the bathroom and lock the door (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 14).
* **Contemporaneous and Third-Party Corroboration:**
  * Ms. Barrett attests that in August 2024, the petitioner called her late at night "crying so hard I could barely understand her," and contemporaneously reported that she and Mr. Lattimore had argued over his taking $600 of rent money from their account, that he had cursed at her and spat in her face, and that she had locked herself in the bathroom (`Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 9).
  * Mr. Reid attests that in 2025, the petitioner cried while recounting to him that Mr. Lattimore had spat on her during an argument (`Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 11).
  * Licensed Clinical Social Worker Gregory T. Hale documents that the petitioner consistently reported the August 2024 spitting incident during clinical therapy sessions and continues to suffer intrusive posttraumatic memories of the event (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, §§ 4–5; p. 3, § 9).
* Because the USCIS Policy Manual explicitly identifies non-consensual **spitting** as an offensive touching constituting **battery** (3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)(1), PDF p. 24 / PM p. 965), and because this incident is credibly detailed by the petitioner and corroborated by three independent sources (including a contemporaneous outcry witness), the record establishes that the petitioner was subjected to battery during the qualifying marriage.

##### B. Finding of Extreme Cruelty
Even independent of the physical battery, the totality of the evidence establishes that Mr. Lattimore subjected the petitioner to **extreme cruelty** between March 2024 and May 2025. Under 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(1)(vi) and 3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)(1) (PDF pp. 23–25 / PM pp. 964–966):
* Extreme cruelty includes "any act or threatened act of violence... which results or threatens to result in physical or mental injury. Psychological or sexual abuse or exploitation... shall be considered acts of violence. Other abusive actions may also be acts of violence under certain circumstances, including acts that, in and of themselves, may not initially appear violent but that are a part of an overall pattern of violence."
* While "[h]urtful conduct alone, or adverse interactions of limited severity, are not sufficient to establish 'extreme' cruelty," conduct rises to the level of extreme cruelty when "[t]he actions... reflect an intention to gain or maintain power and control over the self-petitioner" and endanger the physical or mental health of the spouse (3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)(1), PDF p. 23 / PM p. 964).

Here, the record demonstrates a pervasive pattern of coercive control, psychological degradation, sexual coercion, economic exploitation, and immigration-related intimidation that went far beyond ordinary marital discord:
1. **Weaponization of Immigration Status and Sabotage of Adjustment Proceedings:**
   * As recognized in 3 USCIS-PM D.1(B) (PDF p. 2 / PM p. 943), abusive U.S. citizens often "use their control over this [family-based petitioning] process as a tool to further abuse the alien, threatening to withhold or withdraw the petition in order to control, coerce, and intimidate their family members."
   * Whenever the petitioner complained about Mr. Lattimore's mistreatment, he threatened her immigration status, telling her that she needed him for her green card and that he could have her "sent back to Jamaica whenever he wanted" (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 16; corroborated by `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 11, and `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4).
   * He then acted on these threats by refusing to appear for their scheduled USCIS adjustment of status interview in April 2025 and refusing again to attend the rescheduled interview later that month, asking her, *"Why should I help you get your papers?"* (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 16; corroborated by `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 11; `Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 11; and `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4).
2. **Physical Intimidation, Systematic Verbal Degradation, and Public Humiliation:**
   * After losing his warehouse job in February 2024 and hiding it for three weeks, Mr. Lattimore reacted to the petitioner's inquiry in early March 2024 by jumping up, pointing his finger directly in her face, and shouting so loudly and closely that she backed into the kitchen counter in fear (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 2, ¶¶ 8–9; corroborated by `Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, p. 1, ¶ 9; `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 1, ¶ 6; `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4).
   * Thereafter, he subjected her to ongoing verbal degradation: yelling at her if dinner was not ready when he wanted, pushing his plate away and calling her cooking "slop" and "garbage," telling her she could not do anything right, calling her "stupid," "useless," "worthless," and vulgar epithets, and telling her that no other man would ever want her (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 10).
   * Crucially, this verbal abuse is corroborated by a direct earwitness: Ms. Barrett attests that during numerous Sunday phone calls in the spring and summer of 2024, she personally overheard Mr. Lattimore in the background shouting at the petitioner, calling her "stupid" and "useless," using vulgar profanities, calling her food "slop," and telling her that no other man would ever want her (`Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, pp. 1–2, ¶¶ 6–7; `Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 13). On one Sunday in summer 2024, Mr. Lattimore yelled so loudly that Ms. Barrett heard every word from another room before the petitioner abruptly hung up and called back an hour later in tears (`Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 8).
   * In June 2024, after staying out all night without answering his phone, Mr. Lattimore publicly humiliated the petitioner at his friend Marlon's house in Irvington, screaming at her in front of his laughing friends to "stop embarrassing him and to stop tracking him down like a child," leaving her crying and humiliated (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 11; `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4).
3. **Sexual Coercion:**
   * During this period, Mr. Lattimore demanded sexual relations from the petitioner even when she told him she was exhausted from working long shifts or did not want to participate; when she declined, he responded with anger, sulking, and accusations of infidelity until she relented to avoid conflict (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 12; `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4). Because he was staying out all night and hiding his phone, she felt degraded and feared contracting a sexually transmitted disease, prompting her to visit her physician for testing (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 12).
4. **Economic Control and Financial Exploitation:**
   * Following his termination in February 2024, Mr. Lattimore refused to seek employment and slept until noon while expecting the petitioner to work long shifts as a home health aide, pay all rent and household bills, and perform all cooking, cleaning, and laundry (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 10; `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 10; `Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 11).
   * Although he contributed no income, he exercised control over their joint bank account containing her wages, repeatedly withdrawing cash and lending money to friends (including the $600 rent withdrawal in August 2024) while she struggled to pay rent and utilities (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶¶ 14–15). In early 2025, their joint federal tax refund was seized to satisfy an undisclosed prior debt of Mr. Lattimore's; when questioned, he told her to mind her business and declared that it was *"his name, his money"* (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 15; `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4). On May 17, 2025, he moved out while she was at work, taking the television and furniture and draining most of the remaining funds from their joint account (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 17; `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 12).
5. **Clinically Documented Mental Injury (Psychosocial Assessment Report):**
   * Under 3 USCIS-PM D.2(E)(2) (PDF p. 25 / PM p. 966), psychological evaluations prepared by a qualified mental health professional who treated or thoroughly evaluated the self-petitioner using well-established assessment tools are recognized evidence of battery or extreme cruelty.
   * The Psychosocial Assessment Report (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, pp. 1–4) was prepared by Gregory T. Hale, LCSW (New Jersey License No. `[LICENSE NO.]`), a trauma-focused therapist at Hale Counseling Services, LLC (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, pp. 1, 4). Unlike a single-session forensic evaluation, Mr. Hale treated the petitioner across **eight outpatient therapy sessions** (~9 hours of direct clinical contact between June 12, 2025, and September 18, 2025) following a clinical referral from her primary care physician (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 1, §§ 1–2; `Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, pp. 3–4, ¶ 19).
   * Mr. Hale conducted Mental Status Examinations at each session and administered three well-established, standardized psychometric instruments at intake (06/12/2025) and re-test (09/18/2025):
     * **PHQ-9 (Depression):** Score of 19 at intake (moderately severe) and 14 at re-test (moderate);
     * **GAD-7 (Anxiety):** Score of 15 at intake (severe) and 11 at re-test (moderate); and
     * **PCL-5 (PTSD Checklist for DSM-5):** Score of 49 at intake and 41 at re-test, both substantially above the clinical PTSD threshold of 31–33 (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 1, § 2; p. 3, §§ 6–7).
   * Based on these longitudinal assessments, Mr. Hale diagnosed the petitioner under DSM-5-TR with **Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, moderate (F32.1)** and **Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (F43.10)**, along with **Z69.11 (Encounter for mental health services for victim of spouse or partner psychological abuse)** (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 3, § 8). He documented her severe clinical symptoms—including persistent tearfulness, initial and middle insomnia (4–5 hours of sleep per night), an approximate 15-pound weight loss, social and religious withdrawal, intrusive memories of the August 2024 spitting incident and shouting, exaggerated startle response to raised voices, and physiological hypervigilance upon hearing keys at the apartment door—and concluded that there was no indication of exaggeration or symptom fabrication and that Mr. Lattimore's pattern of psychological abuse and coercive control is the primary cause of her Major Depressive Disorder and PTSD (`Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, pp. 2–3, §§ 5, 9; corroborated by `Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 18; `Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, pp. 1–2, ¶ 10; and `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 2, ¶ 10).
   * In addition, the petitioner reasonably and credibly explained why she did not contact law enforcement during the marriage—citing shame, a belief that police would not intervene in non-visible abuse, and fear that calling the police would escalate the abuse at home and jeopardize her immigration case (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 3, ¶ 19; `Psychosocial_Report_Hale.pdf`, p. 2, § 4). Under the "any credible evidence" standard (3 USCIS-PM D.5(B)(2), PDF p. 53 / PM p. 1014), police reports or protection orders are not required.

#### 7. Good Moral Character (3 USCIS-PM D.2(G)) — **MET**
Under INA § 204(a)(1)(A)(iii)(II)(bb), 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(1)(vii), and 3 USCIS-PM D.2(G)(1)–(3) (PDF pp. 27–31 / PM pp. 968–972), a self-petitioner must demonstrate that she is a person of good moral character, generally focusing on the 3-year period immediately preceding filing, evaluated under INA § 101(f) and the standards of the average citizen in the community. Primary evidence consists of the self-petitioner's affidavit accompanied by local police clearances or state criminal background checks (`USCIS_Policy_Manual_Volume_3_Part_D_VAWA.pdf`, 3 USCIS-PM D.2(G)(3), PDF pp. 30–31 / PM pp. 971–972; 8 CFR § 204.2(c)(2)(v)).
* Pre-review confirmed that the submitted police clearance reports are sufficient to prove the petitioner's good moral character.
* In her affidavit, the petitioner attests under penalty of perjury that she has never been arrested or charged with any crime in the United States or in any other country (`Affidavit_Marcia_Whitfield.pdf`, p. 4, ¶ 20), and Form I-360 confirms that she has never worked in the United States without authorization (`I-360_Whitfield.pdf`, Part 4, Item 6, p. 4).
* Furthermore, both third-party affidavits satisfy the criteria of 3 USCIS-PM D.2(G)(3) (PDF p. 31 / PM p. 972) by providing the affiants' full names, dates and places of birth, U.S. citizenship, residential addresses, telephone numbers, relationships to the petitioner, and long-term personal knowledge of her character (`Affidavit_Desmond_Reid.pdf`, p. 1, ¶¶ 1–3; p. 2, ¶¶ 11, 13 [attesting based on 20 years of friendship that she is "an honest, hardworking, and kind person" whom he has never known to lie]; `Affidavit_Simone_Barrett.pdf`, p. 1, ¶¶ 1–3; p. 3, ¶ 13 [attesting as her first cousin that she is "a truthful, hardworking, and loving person"]). There are no permanent or conditional bars under INA § 101(f) or adverse discretionary factors in the record.
